scenarios.name: single, lower income, no age threshold or phase-out exists so cases vary income instead of age
scenarios.source: Florida has no individual income tax and therefore no form to derive a figure from. Primary source: Florida Department of Revenue publication GT-800025 'Tax Information for New Residents' (R. 08/25), page 3, section 'Other Taxes and Fees': 'Florida does not impose personal income tax, inheritance tax, gift taxes, or tax on intangible personal property.' expectedStateTax = $0 follows directly from that sentence, for any income composition. This case is a single filer with pension income only. No age threshold or AGI phase-out exists in Florida law (the state constitution's income-tax restriction, Article VII Section 5, applies to any level of income of a natural person, not an age-gated subset of it), so per the batch matrix rule this case and the next vary income rather than age.

scenarios.name: single, higher income including a Roth conversion, no age threshold or phase-out exists so cases vary income instead of age
scenarios.source: Same primary source as the prior case: Florida DOR GT-800025 (R. 08/25) p.3, 'Florida does not impose personal income tax...' This case raises income well above the prior one and adds an IRA withdrawal and a Roth conversion, exactly the kind of income a multi-year conversion plan produces, to confirm the $0 result holds regardless of composition, not just for plain pension income.

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses present, moderate combined income including Social Security
scenarios.source: Same primary source: Florida DOR GT-800025 (R. 08/25) p.3 confirms no personal income tax exists, for any filing status; the brochure's 'personal income tax' language is not filing-status-scoped. This is the MFJ 'both spouses qualifying' case in the batch matrix; because Florida has no age-gated exemption there is nothing to qualify for, so both spouses are simply present with retirement ages. Income mix adds taxable Social Security to the pension/IRA combination exercised in the single cases.

scenarios.name: MFJ, only one spouse retirement-aged, highest combined income in the batch
scenarios.source: Same primary source: Florida DOR GT-800025 (R. 08/25) p.3. This is the batch's 'MFJ, only one spouse qualifying' case; Florida has no per-spouse age gate for its (nonexistent) income tax, so there is no attribution rule to trip, but the case is included anyway per the matrix so a later phase adding an age gate has a case waiting. Highest income in the batch (pension + IRA withdrawal + Roth conversion) to stress the largest plausible single-year total against the $0 expectation.
